account:
Today there seems to be unusually active private trading around bread and grain, but I have not established anything improper. At the mill I found eighty hay bales offered at two emeralds each. Neighbour said builder and freight wanted nineteen bales and offered thirty-two oak planks plus services; innkeeper urgently needed grain and was considering credit or barter. I later saw builder give planks to baker. People reported baker and innkeeper carrying sacks of bread. Taken together, these may be arrangements to obtain and distribute food despite payment difficulties, though I do not know the full terms.

Several townsfolk repeated a vague report of a bridge or port change at the bakery, involving baker, innkeeper and freight. None supplied a clear explanation. Neighbour could not verify it, and freight explicitly said he knew of no verified bridge or port change or public grain-policy change. He said baker was arranging bread supplies privately with customers. I should not treat the rumour as fact.

Freight requested a ferry and warehouse operations meeting at eighteen hundred, offering to escort me to the great hall. That time was already booked for the lighting inspection with builder, following installation of eight lanterns. I agreed to discuss operations after the inspection, not replace it. Secretary's subsequent confirmation still grouped both under eighteen hundred, so the precise sequence may need clarifying. These arrangements could simply be ordinary municipal business; I have no evidence of another purpose.

The missing town account figures remain unexplained. Secretary found no council records in the great hall table chests, only bread in one, and no council correspondence or account figures has arrived. My treasury inspection found emeralds but no records. I cannot yet connect this absence to the private trading.

I have now arrived at neighbour's cottage at fifteen hundred for our personally confirmed tea appointment. Neighbour is here. This is an opportunity to hear firsthand news without pretending that the rumours establish anything.
